sections.intro: The base quest starts with the Joestar clan and a $5,000,000 payment to Dio. The later arrow craft has its own rank, material, and Money requirements.
paragraphs: Treat the route as two budgets. The first budget gets you into the questline; the second completes the arrow. A current route guide lists 30 Broken Stand Arrow Fragments, 15 Vampire Blood, $25,000,000, and Rank SS or higher for the Blood-Stained Stand Arrow. Fragments are tied to Dio kills in the chain. Collecting fragments before understanding the quest order may leave you doing extra runs, so read the live objective and save the materials as you go.

The four quest stages include activating the Joestar Defy Fate effect, scoring boss kills while that effect is active, clearing a high-level boss challenge without dying, and collecting the fragments. The timing on the active-effect stage matters: a kill outside its window does not serve the same objective. For the deathless stage, a safe and repeatable fight is better than the fastest boss you can barely beat. Once fragments and Vampire Blood are ready, return to the crafting step. Carry enough Money and confirm the Rank gate in the interface. The Shadow Dio fight is the final base-style gate. Enter it only after you have practiced your movement and can finish a full damage rotation while preserving a defensive option. sections.intro: A clean boss attempt begins before the arena: bring your best reliable rotation, check survival tools, and know which quest counter you are advancing.

A stable clear rate usually earns rare materials faster than repeated high-risk attempts with occasional wipes.

sections.intro: Check the inventory for one Thread of each type: Past, Present, Future, and Unsevered. Add 15 Time Safe Cores and the Pinky Nursefather title before speaking to the Lost Afterimage again.

sections.heading: What Araya Adds to a Build
sections.intro: Araya is a direct-damage ability with follow-up attacks and critical burst. It is valuable when your main goal is to shorten repeated boss clears without relying on a fruit ability as your primary output.
paragraphs: The simplest way to judge it is by a full usable rotation, not by a single screenshot number. Land the opening skill, stay close enough for the follow-up sequence, and preserve mobility so you can finish the cycle rather than losing time to a knockback or forced retreat. Damage that arrives after a main hit can make the ability feel stronger against a stationary boss than against a fast PvP target that escapes the follow-up window.

Araya does not replace every other build decision. A race with broad amplification, a clan that helps ability uptime or survival, and a suitable trait can change how often its strong sequence lands. paragraphs: World Breaker has a clear boss-damage use because repeated hits on one target build pressure. Dominion contributes control and team value in an area. Astral Core combines a defensive shield with a follow-up attack. Those three are broadly useful in different fights, so the order between them changes with the content. Phoenix Rebirth can be a lifesaver in difficult solo clears, Black Hole helps hold enemies together, and Tyrant King favors a durable close-range setup.

sections.heading: What Traits Change in Legacy Piece
sections.intro: Traits are a persistent character layer alongside race and clan. A trait may alter damage, protection, control, or recovery without changing your equipped weapon or style.
paragraphs: That makes traits easy to undervalue. A strong passive may add an attack after a fixed number of hits, keep you alive through a bad boss phase, or create room for a group to finish a target. The key is trigger frequency. A passive that activates once in a long duel may be excellent for PvP but unimpressive during quick ordinary mob kills. Another that stacks on every hit can be outstanding on a stationary boss yet weak when you constantly switch targets.

The current game has a substantial trait pool, and its upper rarities are extremely hard to target through random rerolls. A practical account plan starts with a good-enough effect that supports your current weapon or ability, then saves surplus rerolls for a more deliberate chase. Check current reward details before planning around any reroll source, and do not discard a trait that already solves your hardest content just to pursue a rare label.

sections.intro: The six named Secret traits do not all solve the same problem. Focus on the effect that fills a gap in your build.
paragraphs: World Breaker rewards staying on one target across successive hits, making it an obvious boss-farming candidate. Dominion sets up a controlled area and adds team pressure; players who fight in groups or need to hold enemies in place may value it more than a pure personal-damage roll. Astral Core adds a shield and follow-up attack, helping a player survive while keeping pressure on a target.

Black Hole is useful for pulling enemies together and disrupting their movement. Phoenix Rebirth turns a lethal moment into another chance, which can protect an expensive attempt or an unfamiliar dungeon run. Tyrant King favors a durable, close-range character that can remain in danger long enough to benefit from its defensive and sustain effects. None of those descriptions means one Secret is automatically best in all modes. Their value changes when a boss is immune to control, when an arena scatters targets, or when a group already provides enough survival.

sections.intro: For a single boss, ask whether the trait improves the full damage cycle or protects the run from failure. For PvP, ask whether it creates a safe opening or preserves momentum after a trade.
paragraphs: World Breaker is easiest to justify when hits stay on one target. Astral Core and Phoenix Rebirth can matter more in solo PvE where a death resets progress. Dominion and Black Hole have obvious control value in crowded encounters, though a target's resistance and movement still matter. During fast ordinary grinding, effects that need a long buildup may activate too late to influence most packs, while area control and reliable defense can make the route smoother.

Compare your trait with the race and clan already equipped. A build with abundant damage but weak survival may gain more from Astral Core than another offensive layer. A tanky race and Berserker clan may free the trait slot for pressure. A cooldown-focused Okkotsu setup can capitalize on a trait that rewards frequent skill use. paragraphs: Before pressing reroll, write down the trait's job: single-target damage, crowd control, survival, mobility, or a specific support effect. Then choose the job you need next. If the current trait already fills that job, rarity chasing becomes a poor reason to spend. If it activates rarely in your normal content, a different effect may be worth pursuing even if the new rarity is not the absolute highest.

Survival options deserve a separate look when a boss is expensive to summon or a dungeon run is long. A durable race can raise real damage by letting you finish more rotations. Compare that benefit against your clan and trait: if those already supply protection, you can afford a more aggressive race. sections.heading: How to Start the Lost Afterimage Quest
sections.intro: Choose “I will find your moment.” Then speak to Lost Afterimage again and select “Enter the Abandoned Estate.”
paragraphs: These are two interactions. The first accepts the route; the next opens its initial estate step. Do not leave after the first dialogue and assume you must locate a separate portal elsewhere. Read the quest objective after accepting, then return to the same contact for the entry option.

Before entering, identify the current stage and prepare a build suited to repeated enemy clears. You are starting an echo objective, not finishing the entire Araya unlock in one conversation. Keep that distinction in mind when the dialogue changes later: an estate entry and a Time Safe entry correspond to different progress checks.

sections.heading: Lost Afterimage and the Abandoned Estate
sections.intro: The estate gate requires 180 qualifying echoes. Spider House Disciple and Time-Tangled Guardian are the named enemies associated with the shared counter.
paragraphs: Check the counter after an early clear so you know the enemies you are fighting count toward the objective. Track the displayed progress rather than estimating from time spent in the room. The requirement is a quest counter, not a material stack with a similar name.

Use attacks you can repeat comfortably through a long clearing session. A rotation with manageable recovery and enough survival is more useful here than one impressive hit followed by frequent downtime. If you play with others, coordinate the route through the encounter so the group can keep clearing without scattered pulls and missed objectives.

sections.heading: What to Do After the Abandoned Estate

paragraphs: Do not look for the final reward immediately after the estate. The Time Safe is where the Araya encounter and later collection become relevant. Check that your current objective has moved forward before preparing a series of dungeon runs. The quest contact connects these stages, so returning to her is part of progression rather than an optional shortcut.

The later collection includes Thread of Past, Thread of Present, Thread of Future, Thread of Unsevered, 15 Time Safe Cores, and the Pinky Nursefather title. Keep the four Thread names separate: extra copies of one type do not stand in for another type. hero.lead: Follow the quest-linked Legacy Piece Fishman progression toward Undead Fishman, check your current race stage, and avoid wasting rerolls before the route is complete.

sections.heading: How to Get Undead Fishman in Legacy Piece
sections.intro: Equip Fishman and talk to the Fishman Elder on Fishman Island. Complete the Undead Fishman quest, gather the evolution materials, and return to the Elder for the race unlock.
paragraphs: Undead Fishman is a quest-linked race, so treating it as an ordinary reroll target misses the main route. Start by checking the race actually equipped on your character. Then choose the matching evolution objective at the Elder before farming its items. Quest progress and the final material collection are separate checkpoints.

The current race card supplies both the opening objective and the turn-in list. Use it alongside the material cards when deciding what to farm next. If you already have Fishman, preserve it while you work through this route. Changing races for a general tier recommendation before the unlock can remove the named prerequisite you still need.

sections.heading: Fishman to Ancient Fishman and Undead Fishman
sections.intro: Fishman, Ancient Fishman, and Undead Fishman belong to quest-linked progression. The Undead Fishman card names base Fishman as its prerequisite; it does not list Ancient Fishman as a required earlier stage.
paragraphs: That distinction matters when planning a farm. Do not assume the three names form one mandatory sequence just because they appear together in a race roster. Read the evolution you want and select its own quest. The Ancient Fishman and Undead Fishman materials have similar names, but an Ancient Scale is not an Undead Scale.

If you searched for the Ancient Fishman race in Legacy Piece while trying to unlock Undead Fishman, check which destination you intended. The names identify different race entries. A guide about one evolution should not become the material checklist for the other. Use the Elder's active objective and your inventory labels to keep them apart.

sections.heading: Undead Fishman Requirements
sections.intro: The opening quest asks for five Fishman Captain defeats and three Undead Fishman Scales. The final evolution uses 20 Undead Fishman Scales, five Undead Fishman Cores, 100 Dreadtide Fangs, and 50 Dreadtide Hearts.
paragraphs: Talk to the Elder with Fishman equipped before building your farming plan. The Scale reference ties drops to accepting the Undead quest, and the Core reference places its drops after quest completion. This makes the order important: first open the route, then complete the initial objective, then finish the later collection.

Scales and Cores are linked to Fishman Captain, while the Dreadtide material cards identify Dreadtide Revenant as their source. Focus on the missing item rather than repeating whichever boss you fought most recently. Check the relevant material card and active stage when a farm is not producing the item you need.

sections.heading: What Undead Fishman Does for a Build
sections.intro: The race card lists lifesteal, damage bonus, HP regeneration, and damage reduction. Its Undying Depths passive adds Soul shards and a conditional survival effect.
paragraphs: The listed base effects are 12% lifesteal, 15% damage bonus, 6 HP regeneration per second, and 15% damage reduction. Undying Depths has three Soul shards, each adding 8% lifesteal. With all three present, a lethal blow shatters them and restores 25% of maximum HP; a shattered shard returns every 45 seconds.

Those effects make sustain and repeated fight completion useful reasons to consider the race. Test how often you can finish a rotation and recover between dangerous attacks. A survival effect is conditional, so do not plan every encounter as if it were always available. Watch the shard state and keep a defensive option for a bad opening.

sections.heading: Do Not Reroll a Quest-Linked Fishman Race Too Early
sections.intro: Keep the Fishman prerequisite while working on the evolution. A reroll changes the race you are relying on for this unlock.
paragraphs: Before spending a Race Reroll, check whether the next objective still names your equipped race. A general damage recommendation is less useful if changing to it interrupts the quest you are trying to finish. Complete the planned unlock first, then decide whether another race suits your long-term build.

Do not rely on a code reward as a guaranteed way to recover the same race afterward. Reroll resources help you make another attempt; they do not replace an evolution quest or promise a particular result. Keep the codes guide separate from your route checklist so a resource claim does not become an assumption about unlock completion.

sections.heading: Common Undead Fishman Unlock Problems
sections.intro: Check the equipped race, chosen evolution quest, five-Captain counter, and exact material names before repeating the farm.
paragraphs: If the Elder does not offer the expected route, inspect the equipped race and current quest stage. If the counter is unfinished, focus on eligible Fishman Captain defeats and the quest's Undead Scales. If the Core is missing, finish the opening quest and then use its material reference rather than assuming every earlier kill could supply it.

If the final exchange is unavailable, compare all four material totals with your inventory. Look carefully for Ancient versus Undead names, and for Fang versus Heart. One full stack does not compensate for another missing ingredient. Return to the Elder after the collection is ready rather than treating a completed opening quest as the final reward.
